reviews.text: A harrowing depiction of the Miracle in the Andes that course corrects several Hollywood elements that marred Marshall's Alive back in 1993. The crash sequence is more challenging, and the group's religious beliefs gain prominence.
reviews.author: Joe Lipsett

reviews.text: Bayona uses his many talents as a director to lead his team into a frightening and hopeful place in this survival tale of man against nature.
reviews.author: Nelson Acosta

reviews.text: J.A. Bayona's film captures the horrors of a plane crash in the Andes as well as the resilience of the human spirit.
reviews.author: Udita Jhunjhunwala

reviews.text: This is a hard movie to watch, but that's because it's an honest depiction of a harrowing ordeal.
reviews.author: Rafer Guzman

reviews.text: Society of the Snow rises above a run-of-the-mill survival story.
reviews.author: Barbara Goslawski

reviews.text: Society of the Snow delivers a powerful narrative that transcends the screen, prompting audiences to contemplate the depths of human endurance and compassion in the face of adversity.
reviews.author: Silvia Mariscal

reviews.text: As grisly as it is, given all the horrors and death and cannibalism, the story reassures us that the human will is indeed a mighty thing, and its impact on our desire to live can overcome the seemingly insurmountable.
reviews.author: James Kendrick

reviews.text: As big a part as faith played in their survival, Bayona also keeps focus on the fortitude and sheer luck that shaped this extraordinary and odds-defying tale of endurance.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: Bayona has become a worse director since he made The Impossible in 2012...
reviews.author: A.S. Hamrah

reviews.text: While you’re in the thick of it, Society of the Snow’s horrific immediacy and narrowed and shrunken horizons of survival foregrounded against the limitless, imposing white of the Andean peaks, will have you on the edge of your seat.
reviews.author: Petr Navovy

reviews.text: Bayona ensures this is now the definitive version of this air disaster.
reviews.author: Emma Fraser

reviews.text: The movie could have used more surprises of its kind. Otherwise, Society is a movie I respect more than recommend.
reviews.author: Steve Murray

reviews.text: https://www.ourquadcities.com/news/local-news/cook-review-society-of-the-snow-is-true-life-compelling-tale-of-survival/
reviews.author: Linda Cook

reviews.text: “Society of the Snow” captures the details of this survival story, finding tests of faith and friendship at each turn. It’s an object lesson for Hollywood, that true-life stories can actually be true to life.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: From beginning to end you can’t help but marvel at the characters' resilience and perseverance to simply live, despite everything around them, from plunging temperatures to painful winds, trying to kill them.
reviews.author: Shah Shahid

reviews.text: Magnified by Pedro Luque’s sharp cinematography, this stress-inducing film offers a sensory experience capable of accelerating your heartbeat and diverting your mind from minor troubles.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: [The characters] didn't pop out to me as individual personalities... but as far as the craft of this movie, it's exceptional.
reviews.author: Alonso Duralde

reviews.text: I thought it was super well done, and it was very, very tense.
reviews.author: Christy Lemire

reviews.text: The struggle of those who initially survived the 1972 crash of Uruguayan Air Force Flight 571 in the Andes mountains to remain among the living gets a gripping and emotionally compelling new telling in Society of the Snow.
reviews.author: Mark Meszoros

reviews.text: The film's big set pieces -- the initial crash, the subsequent avalanches -- deliver as much of an adrenaline rush as any action fan could wish. Even more compelling, however, are the quiet scenes of the survivors marking time in the fuselage.
reviews.author: Margot Harrison

reviews.text: The breathtaking film chronicles this astonishing feat of endurance and courage while highlighting the quieter moments of hope and bravery that contributed to the rescue.
reviews.author: Jenn Adams

reviews.text: J.A Bayona manages to create a hymn for the people's willpower, survival and strength in confronting a sure death. That is always worth a watch.  [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: Intense survivalist tale, based on true events, this interpretation is brutally honest about the essential humanity and harsh physicality of the situation that led to cannibalism.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: One of the best movies of the year, Bayona knows how to put the audience as almost another participant of what's happening.  [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Rivera Rubio

reviews.text: Despite Bayona’s sometimes distractingly flashy camerawork, he gives the viewer a sense of authenticity and emotional immediacy about what happened.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: Society of the Snow, director JA Bayona’s take on the 1972 Andes flight disaster, manages to balance out a tight cycle of despair and hope.
reviews.author: Pallavi Keswani

reviews.text: Even with the level of detail that Bayona gives this story, it’s impossible to know what these people went through, especially in their minds. But this filmed version does the best of any of those I’ve seen to capture the trauma its subjects went through.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: Society of the Snow is more gripping and terrifying than any horror story, but in the end, it’s a testament to what human beings can do when they are forced to work together rather than fight one another.
reviews.author: Paul Mount

reviews.text: As a film that attempts to honor its victims while simultaneously offering graphic details, it both improves upon previous iterations of the material and exposes the limits of the story itself.
reviews.author: Shirley Li

reviews.text: This faithful version from Spanish filmmaker J.A. Bayona (The Impossible) is a survival procedural suffused with technical challenges, moral struggle and spiritual reckoning... Bayona has made horror films, but this is not one.
reviews.author: Craig Mathieson

reviews.text:
As an Uruguayan, seeing this film was simultaneously a heartbreaking and a healing experience. An unforgettable celebration of resilience, altruism and the power of stories to keep those that have already departed forever alive. 
[Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Nestor Bentancor

reviews.text: SOCIETY OF THE SNOW is grisly and harrowing, but Bayona treats it with tender diligence and emotional nuance.
reviews.author: JD Duran

reviews.text: For anyone who has seen the previous films, many of the elements will be familiar, but Bayona’s picture manages to make it even more vivid and heartrending without leaning into the sensationalism that marred some of the previous efforts.
reviews.author: Rick Romancito

reviews.text: This historical drama of survival depicting the 1972 Uruguayan air crash disaster in the Andes Mountains might just be the definitive one of more than half a dozen movies and TV documentaries covering this same event.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: Call me crazy, but I do find myself really enjoying these movies about crash survivors resorting to cannibalism. I might have a personality defect.
reviews.author: Bob Grimm

reviews.text: This is a heartbreaking yet uplifting true story that is conveyed in an intensely gripping way. There are moments where viewers will feel every ounce of despair, and this massive mountain range provides a stunning yet horrifying backdrop.
reviews.author: Austin Burke

reviews.text: Bayona’s direction accentuates the personal despair, not the horror. He exposes the danger, making it look formidable, but not insurmountable. The ensemble cast shines under his guidance.
reviews.author: Dwight Brown

reviews.text: Of course, the triumphant survival of fourteen passengers is at the heart of this astounding story. But this is not your standard feel-good fable about the indomitable human spirit triumphing over adversity.
reviews.author: Peg Aloi

reviews.text: The details all come together in a thriller that is so visceral that watching it may very well be the closest most people will ever come to experiencing its central disaster themselves.
reviews.author: Alex Welch

reviews.text: ... After the initial emotional impact, the film will becomes a tedious, predictable slog that didn't need to be 145 minutes long. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Loser

reviews.text: Manages to make the unthinkable feel tangible and the horrific feel personal, taking a true life tale of disaster and treating it as both triumph and tragedy.
reviews.author: Mattie Lucas

reviews.text: An intense, emotional, and visually striking film about brotherhood and the unbreakable human spirit in the face of adversity. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rene Sanchez

reviews.text: Avoids sensationalizing the subject matter but still makes its points.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: Bayona captures, with atmospheres and a certain realism, the harsh conditions of the survivors, but many times I have the feeling that it remains located in a cold terrain that buries the emotion under several layers of snow. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: A gripping survival story filled with emotional moments and impressive technical elements.
reviews.author: Alyssa Christian

reviews.text: A fairly thorough chronicle that is nonetheless never sluggish, and which builds to considerable emotional impact—for me, at least, there are few things more deeply moving than the happiness felt when people finally get a break...
reviews.author: Dennis Harvey

reviews.text: Bayona has made a film about survival that truly places us in the shoes of its characters. He gives every character just enough screen time to make us care and to see the differences in personalities.
reviews.author: Alci Rengifo

reviews.text: It seems to be, at times, excessively anchored in the inherent strength of its historical base and in the facts that already resonate in our collective conscience. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Nicolás Medina

reviews.text: There is a dignity and grace through the film which makes the unthinkable and shocking moments we continually encounter seem plausible and accessible to viewers.
reviews.author: Michael Ward

reviews.text: For all his horror bonafides, however, Bayona has the good sense to never allow Society of the Snow to turn into an exploitation picture. It's a sensitively directed survival drama.
reviews.author: Rohan Naahar

reviews.text: [A] gripping, heart-wrenching look at the emotional toll such an unthinkable event takes on those who somehow came out of it alive, if not exactly well.
reviews.author: Gena Radcliffe

reviews.text: One of the best survivial films ever made. Based on a true story. Nonprofessional cast is superb. Bayona has outdone himself, finally.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: I remember this story in ALIVE (the book) as a kid and it seems it must be retold as a film every gen. This is the most authentic adaptation as you feel every moment of ultimate survival in its native language ... but it needed more than just retelling.
reviews.author: Patrick McDonald

reviews.text: (Bayona) focuses on group dynamics and a collective hunger to survive together, not as each one alone, with the film's large, mostly unknown ensemble delivering on key moments, as well as more than a few moving discussions.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: The film is very straightforward and earnest... And there is something more moving about seeing this performed by people who actually are Spanish and more authentic to the characters.
reviews.author: Amy Nicholson

reviews.text: This is a tough film, not for the faint of heart, but what I was most surprised by was how I became so engaged.
reviews.author: Manuel Betancourt

reviews.text: I was awed by its craftsmanship, less so with its emotion.
reviews.author: Allen Almachar

reviews.text: A human tale of resilience and survival that greatly benefits from a sharp score and a script rooted in firsthand knowledge of the disaster.
reviews.author: Rafaela Sales Ross

reviews.text: The story’s been told before, but Bayona brings a clear-eyed intensity to the story, along with a more authentic Spanish-speaking cast.
reviews.author: Thom Geier

reviews.text: No film could fully capture the awfulness of this experience. But despite some of Bayona’s irksome flair, Society of the Snow does a sturdy enough job getting the point across.
reviews.author: Richard Lawson

reviews.text: Disaster is horror, and Bayona’s direction allows for a deeper comprehension of a tragedy that exists beyond our grasp.
reviews.author: Brianna Zigler

reviews.text: To his huge credit, Spanish director J. A. Bayona presents this intense, harrowing story without any voyeurism, indeed with sensitivity and compassion.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: “Society of the Snow” is a brutal and challenging watch.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: Not since Martin Scorsese's Silence has a film so effectively asked us to consider whether faith is benevolence or a blight.
reviews.author: Roxana Hadadi

reviews.text: A first-rate survival drama that will fray your nerves and touch your heart.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: Shouldn’t a true story of life, death, and cannibalism be a little more gripping?
reviews.author: A.A. Dowd

reviews.text: A stark, haunting adventure, viscerally terrifying, full of despair, informed by the moral and philosophical quandaries of what it takes to sustain oneself in body and spirit in impossible conditions.
reviews.author: MaryAnn Johanson

reviews.text: With fantastic production design, solid marks in all technical aspects, and a compelling narrative that fearlessly allows some nihilism to sneak in amongst the usual "miracle" talk, SOCIETY OF THE SNOW delivers on genre expectations and cinematic scale.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: Bayona's approach allows these philosophical and moral questions space to breathe.
reviews.author: Sheila O'Malley

reviews.text: …well-acted and technically impressive, but it’s also a gruelling watch by design…
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: A story that hinges on the survivors grasping between life and death, Society of the Snow ends with the question of whether or not the tragic and life-changing event was a miracle or tragedy; it is up to the audience to decide.
reviews.author: Nuha Hassan

reviews.text: Bayona makes a point out of naming the victims on screen but falls short of treating his characters like the unique individuals they are.
reviews.author: Lori Meek

reviews.text: Even if we know how this ends, the inevitable catharsis is satisfying.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: Yes, Society of the Snow (La Sociedad de la Nieve) is an inspiring movie about survival against all odds and the power of the human spirit. But to be more specific, it’s a story about how in the darkest times, people find strength in each other.
reviews.author: Lissete Lanuza Sáenz

reviews.text: As earnest as this new production is, whether that’s enough to make the case for watching it once, much less sitting through a reprise for those who have seen “Alive,” feels, frankly, like a pretty tall mountain to climb.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: This is one of the best survival movies I've ever seen. The emotional impact of this incredible real-life survival story is incredible, as it takes us on a journey through the harshest conditions and the resilience of the human spirit.
reviews.author: Elliott Collins

reviews.text: Society of the Snow uses its sound design, setting, and the false security of brief levity to create a deeply upsetting atmosphere... it’s an unbelievable testament to human determination and a survivalist thriller for the ages.
reviews.author: Jason Flatt

reviews.text: A harrowing level of physical and psychological detail.
reviews.author: Siddhant Adlakha

reviews.text: Society of the Snow is realist cinema on a formidable level of execution, yet it’s troubling to think of such formidable technical expertise being used to minutely recreate real-life horror as Sensurround-type spectacle.
reviews.author: Jonathan Romney

reviews.text: Not an easy watch, but a brilliantly-executed real-life drama ... just a great piece of filmmaking by Bayona and all involved.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: [Bayona's] finest film to date, and a fitting tribute to those who both perished and managed to escape their fateful mountain tomb.
reviews.author: Nick Schager

reviews.text: “Society of the Snow” is a perverse movie to watch the way most people will see it — on Netflix, in the comfort of their homes, with a refrigerator nearby.
reviews.author: Ben Kenigsberg

reviews.text: Society of the Snow becomes a humanist experience as much as a traditional survival movie, reaching a sweet spot between brutal visual realism, contained sentimentality and devastating existentialism.
reviews.author: Mireia Mullor

reviews.text: J. A. Bayona’s Society of the Snow has some fascinating, suspenseful set pieces but not much psychological insight or emotional heft.
reviews.author: Hector A. Gonzalez

reviews.text: It may be the best version of this saga told so far. Still, it feels incomplete and doesn’t dig deeper even as it hints at greater pathos beneath the surface.
reviews.author: Courtney Howard

reviews.text: For all the sensationalism of what was a very real ordeal, any accounting of it requires respect, both for the dead and for the living. Mr. Bayona more than meets that standard.
reviews.author: John Anderson

reviews.text: Leaves the viewer cold. ... By keeping his cards tight to his chest, Bayona lays down a technically-impressive and well-intended hand that honors the victims and the survivors with respect. The heart must come later.
reviews.author: Peter Martin

reviews.text: Bayona strips away all sensationalism to best understand the true struggles and sorrows of the survivors, trying to retain as much humanity as possible for a tale that’s primarily known for its most gruesome turns.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: Though “Society of the Snow” has its moments, it’s difficult to see what was gained by telling the story as a dramatic feature.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: ... The strength of Bayona’s film, as its title suggests, are the acts of kindness, sacrifice and love that bind the emaciated, bedraggled survivors together.
reviews.author: Tom Shone

reviews.text: “Society Of Snow” is not only a cinematic feat of wonder, terror, and emotion-stirring courage but a deeply felt portrait of togetherness, brotherhood, and survival, poignantly commemorating the painful memory of indescribable loss and tragedy.
reviews.author: Rodrigo Perez

reviews.text: One of the most immersive films of the year. It is a superb retelling of an incredible story.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: Bayona focuses on the humanity not the sensationalism, showcasing poignant moments of love and care between the characters. It’s a tearjerker at times, sure, but what remains is how much a person can endure under impossible circumstances.
reviews.author: Emily Zemler

reviews.text: “Society of the Snow” pulls no punches with Bayona’s focus on realism. His film is uncomfortably yet respectfully authentic, staying true to every horrific detail without ever being sensational or lurid.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: The tragedy was adapted into the 1993 film Alive, but [director J.A.] Bayona’s interpretation goes beyond sensationalism. Instead, he crafts a thriller that’s both uplifting and awe-inspiring.
reviews.author: Kiko Martinez

reviews.text: One of the most unbelievable, harrowing survival stories ever brought to life by a truly remarkable ensemble cast, breathtaking cinematography, a deeply stirring score, and a plane crash sequence like you’ve never seen before.
reviews.author: Manuel São Bento

reviews.text: “Society of the Snow” is a chilling portrayal of personal fortitude in the face of extraordinary odds.
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: "Society of the Snow" is a “thank your lucky stars” movie. It depicts the kind of true story experience that is frighteningly unfathomable to comprehend. You watch it and reach an overwrought point where all you can do is find gratefulness it wasn't you.
reviews.author: Don Shanahan

reviews.text: Through a series of harrowing events, the film pulls the audience into the emotional complexity of a situation far beyond what we can imagine. It's bracingly involving, riveting and ultimately cathartic.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: Enzo Vogrincic (Numa) and Valentino Alonso (Alfredo), somehow keep the unfathomable and grisly emotive and gripping.
reviews.author: Dulcie Pearce

reviews.text: The visual grandeur and beauty of the shots that Bayona dedicates to the white immensity of the Andes mountain range contrasts head-on with the suffering and despair experienced inside that fuselage. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alicia P. Ferreirós

reviews.text: The power of the film resides in its moral even-handedness and technical virtuosity (the crash is genuinely terrifying).
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: [Bayona] manages to excite us and bring us closer than ever before to the people whose impactful experiences we seem to know frontward and back. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sergio Burstein

reviews.text: Society of the Snow is a respectful yet intense look at tragedy and survival from J.A. Bayona.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: Yet, for all its horrors, “Society of the Snow,” based on Pablo Vierci’s non-fiction book of the same name, is also a story of friendship, sacrifice and hope, and that is what lingers after the film’s nightmares have receded into memory.
reviews.author: Cary Darling

reviews.text: After the initial excitement, the film settles into a tedious, predictable slog that did not need to be 145 minutes long.
reviews.author: Al Alexander

reviews.text: While Society of the Snow’s heart may be in the right place, it’s the individual souls of the people in it that appear to be missing.
reviews.author: Ryan Lattanzio

reviews.text: A retelling that finds in the material more than just a simple tale of the perseverance of the human spirit.
reviews.author: Mark Olsen

reviews.text: If it wouldn't be absolutely terrifying to do so, Society of the Snow feels like the exact type of movie you'll watch alone on a plane a few months from now and find it to be quite good before bemoaning that it didn't get a wider theatrical release.
reviews.author: Chase Hutchinson

reviews.text: Based on the book of the same name by Uruguayan Pablo Vierci published in 2009, the film moves away from the exploitation of the tragedy to focus on the analysis of its witnesses. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Aglaia Berlutti

reviews.text: Realism defines the film - actors lost weight and became oddly at one with the cold, there’s a kind of majesty, a heightened sense of soul, that those who know they may die, might feel an appreciation of life. And that is one heck of a crash sequence.
reviews.author: Anne Brodie

reviews.text: Society of the Snow tells this story with bluntness, thoughtfulness, and respect...
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: Society of the Snow is a gripping tale that takes you through a cascade of emotions.
reviews.author: Joseph Robinson

reviews.text: Society of the Snow works as a stripped-down survival epic, but its moral questions are as stark, alarming, and real as the rugged peaks that trapped those who lived through the crash.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: Society of the Snow's closing exhortation to keep taking care of each other is all too easily lost in the blizzard that is modern life, and the best of messages in any year. True North will be easier to find after watching.
reviews.author: Harry Guerin

reviews.text: The crash itself is superbly recreated and there’s an eerie beauty to Bayona’s depiction of the snowy wilderness that felt like hell but looked like heaven.
reviews.author: Paul Whitington

reviews.text: A visceral, tasteful, impeccably crafted look at the horrors of an unforgiving situation and a triumph of the human spirit through unity
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: Society of the Snow is wrenching, deeply harrowing, but crucially dispenses with sappy takeaways about the triumph of the human spirit.
reviews.author: Tim Robey

reviews.text: From its nerve-shredding crash sequence to the breathtaking and unforgiving locations, Bayona has delivered a robust and riveting retelling of this extraordinary and unfathomable experience.
reviews.author: James Marsh

reviews.text: The film takes the trouble to seek answers with genuine emotion and dramatic complexity... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Juanma Fernández París

reviews.text: A viscerally rendered plane crash gives way to an affecting story of humanity and survival. Bayona is on impressive form here.
reviews.author: Amon Warmann

reviews.text: Often thrilling, engrossing and well-shot, but conventional and just mildly engaging.
reviews.author: Avi Offer

reviews.text: There are some smart filmmaking choices here... But there is also a going-through-the-motions quality to the film, as though its only real purpose was to present this tale from a non-American point of view.
reviews.author: Andrew Dignan

reviews.text: This is a fervent film, heartfelt and shot with passion and sweep.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: A breathtaking motion picture that enthralls across the length of its 140+ minute running time.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: Society of the Snow is the work of someone passionate enough that every brutal minute of the film feels like it was made with immense care and respect, which elevates the film beyond the depths of lurid melodrama into something painfully human.
reviews.author: Holly Hazelwood

reviews.text: While it is a thrilling survival adventure on the one hand, it in no way exploits its victims, instead illuminating the intense spiritual bond that quickly grew among them, one in which friends would offer up their deaths to the living…
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: A film that is as heartfelt as it is beautifully realized. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carlos Boyero

reviews.text: J.A. Bayona rarely lets his images speak for themselves, which is frustrating given his obvious gift for poetic, almost surreal succinctness.
reviews.author: Steven Nguyen Scaife

reviews.text: It will generate emotional reactions in the viewer, without being afraid to show everything it has to show. “Society of the Snow” is one of the best things Bayona has done; an intense, emotional and powerful survival film. Full review in Spanish.
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: Bayona recovers the old and noble breath of the classics to tell the definitive story of the Andes tragedy that occurred in 1972... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Marcelo Stiletano

reviews.text: The problem with Society of the Snow is its duration... Especially when we already know what will happen. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: Bayona manages the right balance between what she should and should not show, without falling into the lurid, but without hiding a sad and sinister reality. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Philipp Engel

reviews.text: Seeing Bayona work hard to keep the details intact and sticking close to all involved, it really feels like an up-close and personal look at a tragic event that never betrays authenticity.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: The Society of Snow functions as a canvas on the verge of abstraction, populated by extreme close-ups that eloquently capture the desperation and desire for survival... we could think of The Scream, by Edvard Munch. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Manu Yáñez

reviews.text: The largely unknown cast are excellent, the special effects seamless, and Bayona has a real talent for showing spectacle on a human scale. The result is inspiring, emotive and, in places, shocking, even for those who might think they know the whole story.
reviews.author: Matt Glasby

reviews.text: film boasts a fantastic ensemble led by an excellent Enzo Vogrincic...Bayona manages a nuanced exploration of how, when a group come to truly care about one another and work together, the impossible becomes possible—a message we profoundly need right now.
reviews.author: Frank J. Avella

reviews.text: I don’t expect that this story will be told on “film” again in this generation. This film is pretty much the definitive telling. A masterwork. Can’t get more honest about the humanity or the cannibalism or the physicality of the situation.
reviews.author: David Poland

reviews.text: Michael Giacchino’s exceptional score, resonating almost reverently with the tragic events that claimed 29 lives, enhances the film’s emotional impact. Pedro Luque’s breathtaking cinematography adds a layer of intensity to the incredible tale of survival.
reviews.author: Mark Johnson

reviews.text: A movie that it's very much the work of Bayona. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Erick Estrada

reviews.text: Society of the Snow proves that the capacity to move and excite audiences can be genuine without the need for manipulation. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Juan Pablo Russo

reviews.text: “Society of the Snow” is a captivating true-life disaster film that exceeds on every technical level.
reviews.author: Giovanni Lago

reviews.text: Society of the Snow contains all the thrills and masterclass filmmaking cinephiles expect in a great survival drama, but it’s the simple yet profound message that resonates the most.
reviews.author: Alex Saveliev

reviews.text: The impact of the plane crash near the start of this retelling of the remarkable true survival story is shown in visceral detail with a sound design that slams right through you..
reviews.author: Amber Wilkinson

reviews.text: A more authentic take on this incredible tale of survival and strength of the human spirit.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: Bayona films following a catalog of rules that allows the viewer to suffer. The specialty of his cinema is having the viewer suffer in front of a screen while playing excessively with their emotions. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Àngel Quintana

reviews.text: Bayona's attention to detail on the realism and setting high up in the Andes mountains makes it absolutely entrancing to watch. If only everyone could experience it in a cinema.
reviews.author: Alex Billington

reviews.text: The editing goes far beyond what is required of a biopic: the moment of the fall, narrated from the point of view of an eye and its subsequent silence, is one of the best in the history of disaster cinema... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Randy Meeks

reviews.text: Society of the Snow is careful to memorialise the dead in a moving, meaningful way.
reviews.author: Philip De Semlyen

reviews.text: Competently made and worth seeing.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: Uneven but ultimately effective.
reviews.author: David Rooney

reviews.text: Society of the Snow dazzles us in many ways. Everything is as credible as it's devastating. And claustrophobic. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Tommaso Koch

reviews.text: A display of cinema that is as emotional as it is spectacular despite its problems with narration and rhythm. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Luis Martínez

reviews.text: This is ultimately a spiritual journey on many levels, focusing on the human will to overcome the worst of circumstances.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: "[Society of the Snow] will definitely make you reconsider any imminent flight plans – not a good thing if you’re at an international film festival."
reviews.author: Matthew Turner

reviews.text: Grips with alternating waves of dread, horror and heart-swelling relief, even as it can hardly surprise.
reviews.author: Guy Lodge

reviews.text: J.A. Bayona’s adaptation of this much-filmed story is elevated by bracingly muscular action sequences.
reviews.author: Wendy Ide

synopsis: In 1972, Uruguayan Air Force Flight 571, which had been chartered to fly a rugby team to Chile, crashed in the heart of the Andes. Only 29 of its 45 passengers survived the accident. Trapped in one of the most hostile and inaccessible environments on the planet, they have to resort to extreme measures to stay alive.
